posts.author: wler
posts.content_md:
Some while ago there was some discussion about

using this gadget

[http://www.panavise.com/nf/vises/vises_cbholders.html](http://www.panavise.com/nf/vises/vises_cbholders.html)

as a film or plate holder. 

Does anybody have practrical experience with it, in the mean while?

Is it stable enough, and easy to handle in the dark? Can the center

rod be removed (for mounting on a custom base)?

I need to switch to an adjustable holder, for trying different format.

Thanks for answers !

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
This looks like the new improved version of what I have used. The old one you could take off the center post. The only trick is to use just enough pressure from the spring-loaded side to hold the plate without putting stress on it. 

It was designed for PCB's, and worked fine for the old 1.5 mm thick Agfa Glass, but the grooves on the sides of the blades might have a problem with thicker glass.

posts.author: wler
posts.content_md:
Thanks !

They write something about 4mm max plate thickness - this should be

enough for plates, but probably not for film-sandwiches between 2

glass plates. So, it the thing stable enough ? The thin arms make

me a bit worry, I normally use more heavy stuff.

posts.author: aghisays
posts.content_md:
I use one of those in my H2 copy setup for holding the master with good results. When I was using it with film-sandwiches I got missed results because the grooves are too small and with long exposures I got film movement. Now that I'm using film laminated to glass (2mm glass) it works really well even with long exposures (2 min or more).

Andres.

posts.author: eric343
posts.content_md:
It's great for use with plates -- it's incredibly stable. You do need a sturdy way of mounting it; it won't work on sand tables unless you're willing to accept some shifting around while inserting and removing the plate.

It can be used with sandwiched film, but I wouldn't recommend it. It's a hassle.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md:
> **aghisays:** Now that I'm using film laminated to glass (2mm glass) it works really well even with long exposures (2 min or more).Andres.

what fluid are you using to index your film to the glass?

posts.author: aghisays
posts.content_md:
I don't index match. At least not with liquids. I laminate the film to glass using the same laminating material mentioned by MichaelH in some other posts. He gave me some of his to try out. I don't have the information handy but I soon as he is back from his business trip I will post it.

Maybe a search will help in the mean time.

Andres.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
I use the OPCLR material from Kapco and laminate film to glass for my transmission masters. I generally haven't done much with the reflections because of paranoia about dust getting between the film and glass. Once the film is down, you can't remove it without ruining the film and image.

For masters this is less of a concern because a single speck of dust generally won't ruin a master.
